title: Frontend Reactivation & Full-Stack Surface Analysis: radblok.co.za Live Audit
summary: Following domain reactivation by registrar xneelo and service resumption on Render, conducted live Layer 7 reconnaissance against the restored production frontend at https://radblok.co.za. Mapped application routing structure (/dashboard, /admin, /register, /post/:id), audited session cookie security (connect.sid), and evaluated missing HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options) across the live edge.

blocks.text: Earlier in Entry 012, `radblok.co.za` returned `HTTP 503 Service Unavailable` with `x-render-routing: suspend-by-user`. Following registrar account unlocking and service unsuspension in Render, live HTTP probes confirmed the frontend is back online with full Cloudflare edge termination at the Cape Town PoP (`CPT`):

The apex domain `radblok.co.za` cleanly issues a 301 redirect to canonical `https://www.radblok.co.za/`, where Render responds in `200 OK`.
Automated HTML parsing of internal navigational links and form actions revealed the public and restricted route tree:

head: Route / Endpoint
HTTP Method
Access Level
Observed Behavior & Technical Purpose
rows: Homepage delivering published articles, branding, and author overview.
Informational site and author background page.
Dynamic post viewer querying MongoDB by 24-character ObjectID (e.g., `/post/6780f110c998d75dd1cea1ac`).
Protected member area. Returns `HTTP 302 Found` redirecting unauthenticated requests directly to `/admin`.
Authentication portal hosting `<form action="/admin" method="post">` with username and password inputs.
Content publishing form for authenticated authors.

blocks.text: The application issues an Express session cookie upon first interaction: `Set-Cookie: connect.sid=...; Path=/; HttpOnly`.

head: Cookie Attribute
State
Security Assessment
rows: **Positive**: Prevents client-side scripts from reading `document.cookie`, mitigating credential theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
**Defect**: The cookie lacks the `Secure` flag. Browsers may transmit this session token over unencrypted HTTP if the user enters `http://` before HTTPS redirection occurs.

**Defect**: Without `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict`, the browser attaches `connect.sid` to cross-site requests, exposing authenticated state-changing actions (e.g. creating/deleting posts) to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF).

blocks.text: Probing response headers against the OWASP Secure Headers Project identified critical omissions:

head: Header
Status
Vulnerability / Exploit Potential
rows: Browsers are not forced to connect via HTTPS on future sessions; vulnerable to SSL-stripping MITM.
Allows embedding within an external `<iframe>`, creating an active **Clickjacking** vector on the `/admin` login form.
No domain restrictions for scripts or styles; increases severity of potential stored or reflected XSS.
Permits MIME-sniffing, where browsers execute uploaded non-script files as scripts.
Reveals server framework to automated scanners and fingerprinting engines.
